info.title: dotnet-csverify
info.description: The CsVerify verifier: proves C# code's CsVerify specifications (contracts, loop invariants, termination, views) with Z3, and erases the proofs. Run "dotnet csverify", or build with -p:CsVerifyEnabled=true.

options.name: --no-overflow
options.description:
treat every integer as mathematical (unsound where code can overflow); by default
run-time arithmetic is C#'s: overflow is reported unless checked (throws) or
unchecked (wraps on purpose)

options.name: --nullable
options.description:
nullable context: enable (default), disable, annotations, warnings; only
non-nullable reference types are known not to be null

options.name: --timeout
options.description: per-query Z3 timeout (default 10000)

options.name: --cores
options.description: solvers run side by side (default: one a core, at most one per 4 GB of memory)

options.name: --z3
options.description: Z3 executable (default: CSVERIFY_Z3, then PATH)

options.name: --cache
options.description:
keep the methods proved in this file, and don't prove one again while nothing its proof
depends on has changed (the MSBuild target keeps it in obj/)

options.name: --assembly-name
options.description:
the program's assembly name (the project's, which the MSBuild target passes), so
that the internals InternalsVisibleTo grants it are visible

options.name: -d
options.description: extra preprocessor symbol (CSVERIFY_SPEC is always defined)

options.name: -r
options.description: extra metadata reference

options.name: -a
options.description:
run the source generators of this analyzer assembly on the program (generated
code is compiled, not verified)

options.name: --analyzer-config
options.description: an .editorconfig or .globalconfig the generators read

options.name: --project-reference
options.description:
a referenced project, as its build describes it (repeatable; the MSBuild target
passes them): compiled as a project of its own, which the program's references, so
that its code is the program's; called by its contracts, not verified

options.name: --only
options.description:
verify only the methods whose name (Type.Method, or Outer.Type.Method) contains the
text (repeatable); the others are called by their contracts, not verified

options.name: -v
options.description:
list every method with its proved obligations, and the library contracts
([ContractsFor] stubs, trusted) the proofs assumed

options.name: --ef-static-model
options.description:
read an EF Core model from the sources only, without loading the program to ask
EF for its own (which runs the contexts' constructors and model configuration)

options.name: --native
options.description:
a native library the program's packages bring (repeatable; the MSBuild targets
pass them): what a database provider loads where EF's model is built

options.name: --checks
options.description:
prove only these kinds of obligation, a comma-separated list of null, linear,
bounds, overflow, contracts (or all); the others are assumed, and counted.
Within a profile an unsupported construct is a warning, its value unknown, and
a method not verified (CSV1902) a warning too, counted

options.name: --each
options.description:
verify each argument as a program of its own (a comma joins paths into one), and
combine the results: for programs that cannot be compiled together

options.name: --library-report
options.description:
after the results, rank what the failures come from: library members without
contracts (by the failures they cause, and their calls), methods without
postconditions, loops without invariants; and the failures by kind, the
unsupported constructs and the unknown values

options.name: --help
options.description:
this text
csverify erase --out <dir> ...   writes the program with every proof erased (csverify erase -h)
